    Create an sm_corpus object

    Source: R/corpus-class.R, R/corpus-coerce.R, R/corpus-print.R
    sm_corpus.Rd

    Build a typed, tibble-of-tibbles corpus container for bibliometric analysis. The corpus is the central data structure in scimapR, holding works, authors, authorships, institutions, sources, references, concepts, embeddings, provenance, screening decisions, and metadata.

    Usage

    sm_corpus(
  works,
  authors = NULL,
  authorships = NULL,
  institutions = NULL,
  sources = NULL,
  references = NULL,
  concepts = NULL,
  embeddings = NULL,
  provenance = NULL,
  screening = NULL,
  metadata = list()
)

    Arguments

    works

    A tibble of works (publications). See Details for schema.

    authors

    A tibble of authors. If NULL, constructed from works.

    authorships

    A tibble linking works to authors. If NULL, empty.

    institutions

    A tibble of institutions. If NULL, empty.

    sources

    A tibble of publication sources/journals. If NULL, empty.

    references

    A tibble of cited references. If NULL, empty.

    concepts

    A tibble of concepts/keywords. If NULL, empty. Legacy and common spellings in its vocabulary column (such as "keywords-author") are renamed to the names of sm_concept_vocabularies(), with a message. Values that name no known vocabulary are kept as written and listed in the same message, each time a corpus is built from them; name a vocabulary of your own "custom".

    embeddings

    A numeric matrix of work embeddings, or NULL.

    provenance

    A tibble tracking data lineage. If NULL, empty.

    screening

    A tibble of screening decisions. If NULL, empty.

    metadata

    A list of corpus-level metadata.

    x, object

    An sm_corpus object.

    i

    Row index for subsetting.

    ...

    Ignored.

    Value

    An sm_corpus S3 object.

    • [: An sm_corpus with the selected works.

    • length(): Number of works (integer).

    • dim(): Integer vector of length 2 (rows, columns of works table).

    • as_tibble(): The works tibble.

    • as.data.frame(): The works table as a data frame.

    • print(): x invisibly.

    • format(): A single character string.

    • summary(): A named list of summary statistics.

    • str(): object invisibly.

    Details

    A corpus is a list of tables that share identifiers: work_id links every table to works, author_id links authorships to authors, institution_id links them to institutions and source_id links works to sources. The tables below list, for each element, the required columns, which the readers and fetchers always write (a value may be NA), and the optional columns that some readers and functions write or read. sm_corpus() adds the missing required columns of works (mostly NA); it takes the other tables as given.

    works: one row per work. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    work_idcharacterIdentifier, unique within the corpus
    doicharacterDOI, lower case, without https://doi.org/
    title, abstractcharacterTitle and abstract
    yearintegerPublication year
    typecharacterDocument type, as the source names it
    source_idcharacterThe journal or other source (sources)
    cited_by_countintegerCitations, as the source counts them
    oa_statuscharacterOpen-access status
    languagecharacterLanguage
    pmid, arxiv_id, openalex_idcharacterOther identifiers
    is_retractedlogicalRetraction flag
    retraction_dateDateDate of the retraction
    last_refreshedPOSIXctWhen the record was read or fetched

    Optional: quartile, jif_quartile or sjr_quartile (journal quartiles such as "Q1", for sm_its(outcome = "share_q1")); cnci, fnci, rcr and other impact columns (see sm_its()); field (for sm_metric_fnci(classification = "manual")); citation_mature and cnci_provisional (sm_citation_maturity()); cluster_id and cluster_label (the clustering functions).

    authors: one row per author. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    author_idcharacterIdentifier, unique within the corpus
    orcidcharacterORCID iD
    display_namecharacterName
    display_name_alternativeslist of characterOther spellings
    inferred_gender, gender_methodcharacterGender and its method
    gender_confidencedoubleConfidence of inferred_gender

    display_name_alternatives holds, for example, the names as a Web of Science file writes them, and sm_audit_gender(method = "manual") reads the gender columns. Optional: none so far.

    authorships: one row per work, author and affiliation, so an author with several addresses in a work has several rows, which share position and is_corresponding. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    work_id, author_idcharacterThe work and the author
    positionintegerPlace in the author list, from 1 (NA: unknown)
    is_correspondinglogicalCorresponding author: see below
    institution_idcharacterThe institution (institutions)
    raw_affiliationcharacterThe address as the source writes it
    country_codecharacterISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code

    is_corresponding is TRUE for the authors the source names as corresponding, FALSE for the other authors of such a work and NA when the source does not say who the corresponding author is. sm_read_wos() and as_sm_corpus() read it from the RP field, sm_read_openalex_json() and sm_fetch_openalex() from OpenAlex (a work whose authors are all marked false takes its corresponding authors from corresponding_author_ids, and counts as unknown when that lists none of them), sm_read_dimensions() from its Corresponding Authors column and sm_fetch_biorxiv() from the bioRxiv API; the other readers and fetchers write NA. Up to scimapR 0.4.0 they flagged the first author instead. A name that fits several authors of a work equally (namesakes with the same surname and initials) and that the source does not tell apart leaves them NA. Functions that select corresponding authors take TRUE only, and the leadership outcome of sm_its() leaves works whose corresponding author is unknown out of its shares.

    Optional: institution_match, match_method, match_signal and match_evidence (sm_affiliation_match()); institution_name (sm_attribute_institution()); email (exported as EM by sm_to_bibliometrix()).

    institutions: one row per institution. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    institution_idcharacterIdentifier, as in authorships
    rorcharacterROR id
    display_namecharacterName
    country_codecharacterISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code
    region, income_tiercharacterWorld region and income group
    typecharacterKind of institution, such as education or healthcare

    Optional: none so far.

    sources: one row per journal or other source. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    source_idcharacterIdentifier, as in works
    issn_lcharacterLinking ISSN
    issnlist of characterAll ISSNs of the source
    display_namecharacterName
    typecharacterKind of source, such as journal
    is_oalogicalOpen-access source
    publisher, publisher_countrycharacterPublisher and its country

    Optional: abbreviation and iso_abbreviation (character; the Web of Science abbreviations J9 and JI, written by sm_read_wos() and the bibliometrix conversion and exported by sm_to_bibliometrix()).

    references: one row per cited reference. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    work_idcharacterThe citing work
    ref_indexintegerPlace in the work's reference list
    cited_work_idcharacterThe cited work, when it is in works
    cited_doicharacterDOI of the cited work
    cited_rawcharacterThe reference as the source writes it

    Optional: none so far.

    concepts: one row per keyword, category or concept of a work. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    work_idcharacterThe work
    concept_idcharacterIdentifier in its vocabulary
    concept_namecharacterThe keyword, category or concept
    levelintegerLevel in the hierarchy of the vocabulary
    scoredoubleWeight given by the source
    vocabularycharacterOne of sm_concept_vocabularies()

    For MeSH headings score is 1 for a major topic and 0 otherwise. Optional: none so far.

    embeddings: NULL or a numeric matrix with one row per work, named by work_id.

    provenance: one row per work and source. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    work_idcharacterThe work
    sourcecharacterWhere the record comes from, such as "wos"
    source_id_externalcharacterIts identifier at the source
    fetch_datePOSIXctWhen it was read or fetched
    querycharacterThe query or file it came from
    enginecharacterThe parser or client that read it
    scimapR_versioncharacterThe scimapR version that read it
    prompt_hashcharacterHash of a prompt behind the record

    source_id_external is, for example, the Web of Science accession number (UT); prompt_hash is NA for records that no prompt produced. Optional: none so far.

    screening: one row per screening decision. Required:

    ColumnTypeContent
    work_idcharacterThe work
    stagecharacterStage, such as "title-abstract" or "full-text"
    decisioncharacter"include", "exclude" or "unclear"
    reasoncharacterReason for the decision
    confidencedoubleConfidence of the decision
    sourcecharacterWho or what decided
    decided_atPOSIXctWhen

    Optional: none so far.

    metadata: a list. Required:

    EntryTypeContent
    scimapR_versioncharacterThe scimapR version that built the corpus
    build_datePOSIXctWhen the corpus was built
    corpus_hashcharacterHash of the content (sm_hash_corpus())
    is_lockedlogicalWhether sm_lock() locked the corpus
    last_refreshPOSIXctWhen sm_refresh() last ran
    question_idcharacterId of its sm_question()

    question_id is set by sm_corpus_for_question(). Optional: entries the readers add, such as source_file and reader. build_date and last_refresh may also be numbers of seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, as corpora restored from tables store them, ISO 8601 text or dates; sm_certificate() and the citation-maturity cut-offs read all of these.

    See also

    Other corpus: as_sm_corpus(), is_sm_corpus(), sm_bind_corpora(), sm_build_corpus(), sm_concept_vocabularies(), sm_corpus_from_tables(), sm_dedupe(), sm_materialise(), sm_save_corpus(), sm_validate(), validate_sm_corpus()

    Examples

    corpus <- sm_corpus(
  works = tibble::tibble(
    work_id = "W000000001",
    doi = "10.1234/example",
    title = "Example Work",
    abstract = "An example abstract.",
    year = 2024L,
    type = "journal-article",
    source_id = NA_character_,
    cited_by_count = 0L,
    oa_status = "closed",
    language = "en",
    pmid = NA_character_,
    arxiv_id = NA_character_,
    openalex_id = NA_character_,
    is_retracted = FALSE,
    retraction_date = NA_real_,
    last_refreshed = Sys.time()
  )
)
print(corpus)
#> 
#> ── <sm_corpus> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Works: 1 | Authors: 0 | Institutions: 0
#> Years: 2024 - 2024
#> Sources (journals): 0
#> Embeddings: none
#> Status: Unlocked (last refreshed: never)
